title.narrative: Punjab Urban Land Systems Enhancement Project

description.narrative: The Government of Pakistan has initiated several pro-poor programs, including the Naya Pakistan Housing Program (NPHP). Launched in April 2019, NPHP seeks to build five million low-cost housing units in urban areas across the country within a five-year timeframe. Access to land with secure tenure is a basic requirement for sustainable and affordable housing. Although information on urban property transactions is typically recorded through the registration of deeds, a standardized methodology for transaction processing does not exist in the urban areas of Punjab. Given the existing gaps and the absence of a standardized system of recording property rights in urban areas, the following challenges persist: (i) property tax evasion and inequitable taxation; (ii) non-availability of formal ownership records; (iii) lengthy dispute resolution and litigation processes; (iv) overlapping record registries in multiple agencies that lack harmonization; (v) lack of easy access to property rights information for development authorities to fulfill their core functions; and (vi) absence of up-to-date cadastral data for government agencies to incorporate climate change considerations. Women in urban areas also face marginalization and the loss of inheritance rights to land due to the lack of clarity on property ownership, limited access to land-related services, and cultural restrictions. As such, the Project will support the creation of a province-wide digital cadastral map, standardization and interlinking land records, data improvement in urban and rural areas, the scale-up of Land Record Management and Information System (LRMIS), as well as project management and policy development. Promoting a more transparent, efficient, and selective supply of land will address one of the critical bottlenecks to the supply of affordable housing. The Project Components are: Component 1: Digital Land Records and Cadastral Maps for LRMIS - Subcomponent 1.1: Spatial framework for LRMIS; Subcomponent 1.2: Systematic registration of peri-urban properties; Subcomponent 1.3: Upgrading tax records to urban land records; Subcomponent 1.4: Incorporation of existing urban records into a unified land registry; and Subcomponent 1.5: Systematic registration of urban properties. Component 2: Land for Housing - Preparing an inventory of state lands and supporting the Project Implementing Entity to develop strategies and procedures for managing those public land asset.Component 3: Integrated Land and Geospatial Information Systems and Services - Subcomponent 3.1: ICT Infrastructure upgrade; Subcomponent 3.2: LRMIS improvement; Subcomponent 3.3: Integrated land portal; and Subcomponent 3.4: Establishing a provincial spatial data infrastructure.Component 4: Project Management and Institutional Strengthening.
The objectives of the Project are to support the Government of Punjab with: (i) improved land records; and (ii) identification of land for development, including land for housing programs.

title.narrative: Districts with new LRMIS in use with online connection to a centralized database

comment.narrative: Although the 2025 target of covering 8 districts has not been met, the project is expected to exceed the original end target by covering 38 districts—two more than the initially planned 36—by the end of implementation. The project is on track to meet the end target.

This indicator measures the number of cities with enhanced capacity for revenue generation. Progress will be made once the updated land records are shared with sub-national government through the next-generation LRMIS.

title.narrative: Baseline, mid-term and final project impact evaluations

comment.narrative: A baseline survey was conducted from December 2023 to January 2024. A midline survey is underway at MTR. The end target is expected to be achieved.

title.narrative: Landowners whose land records newly registered and/or updated in LRMIS

comment.narrative: The PLRA has updated/registered revenue records of 10,426,698 landowners in the LRMIS by implementing mouza digitization, reconstruction of mouza, and parcel mapping in Phase 1 and 2 districts. This significant increase is driven by additional investments in the digitalization of Mouzas, as well as the deployment of ICT support across all Arazi Record Centers and Qanoongoes (210 sites).

The total number of beneficiaries who received training in GIS tasks, field surveys, and E&S safeguard is 2,570 at MTR. Of which, 31.6 percent (812 trainees) are women. The project slightly exceeded the 2025 target of training 2,500 people. The workplan has been revised to set a more ambitious end target, increasing the goal by an additional 500 trainees.

title.narrative: Person-based records converted to parcel-based records in LRMIS

comment.narrative: The number of parcel-based records increased to 25.3 million. Progress to date has significantly exceeded expectations, reaching nearly twice the original 2025 target. The number of records currently being processed is projected to reach 32,000, well above initial estimates.

title.narrative: Progress of the state lands asset inventory

comment.narrative: Digitizing, correcting, and validating state land data have been conducted to cover 35 out of 41 districts in Punjab. The current progress on the state land asset inventory stands at 51.09%, which is approximately 15% above the 2025 target of 35%. The end target has been confirmed as realistic and achievable.

title.narrative: Coverage of image base maps provided by PSDI for mapping and DRM

comment.narrative: The Project has created base maps, which include drone and satellite imagery, covering about 105,362 sq.km. The achievement of 51.31% at MTR falls short of the 2025 target of 63%. Projections for intermediate and end targets still remain realistic.

title.narrative: Increased coverage of updated digital cadastral maps

comment.narrative: The coverage of digital maps increased to 66.1 percent (89,266 sq.km) of the total project project area. PULSE exceeded its end target by covering nearly 4.3% more of the provincial area with updated digital maps than originally planned. This achievement was driven by the efficiency of the technical PULSE PIU and PMU teams, along with active private sector involvement, which accelerated progress and raised the estimated coverage to 85%.

The project has implemented cadastral surveying in 10 divisions of Punjab, covering a total of 82,364 ha. Progress at the MTR stage falls significantly short of the original 2025 target of 424,000 hectares for cadastral surveying. Following a more realistic assessment, taking into account the actual area to be covered by parcel surveys (field measurements) and the challenges of land registration in urban center areas, has led to a substantial downward revision of the end target upon the proposed project restructuring.

title.narrative: External land records incorporated into LRMIS

comment.narrative: Digitization of urban land records and maps has been implemented in collaboration with private housing societies and seven external development authorities, including Cooperative Housing Authority Punjab, PHATA, LDA, FDA, RDA, MDA, and GDA. Due to fewer number of private housing societies being integrated than originally designed, the significant revision of this indicator's end target is needed, which has been reduced from 4,374 to 2,187 land records incorporated into LRMIS. To address this challenge, the project will implement measures to encourage private housing societies and urban residents to register their parcels and increase investment in awareness and media campaigns.

title.narrative: Electronic requests processed annually by LRMIS

comment.narrative: The progress exceeded the 2025 target of 1,331, with measurements conducted annually each September This indicator is assessed annually in September. The end target is expected to be achieved.

title.narrative: Reduction in average time to register a property transaction

comment.narrative: This indicator will measure the progress (reduction in time) in registering a property by the average number of days through mid-line and end-line surveys. The end target is to reduce the time from the baseline of 22.5 days to 15 days.

title.narrative: Area of public lands screened for housing

comment.narrative: The indicator measures the area of public lands identified and screened for potential development, including housing program. The progress has already surpassed the 2025 target and is on track to meet both the intermediate and final targets as projected.

title.narrative: LRMIS user satisfaction with land administration services

comment.narrative: LRMIS user satisfaction with land administration services (e.g., mutation and fard issuance) is 69 percent based on the baseline survey. The achievement at the MTR is approximately 5% below the 2025 target of 75.6. Nevertheless, projections indicate that both the intermediate and final targets will be successfully met.

title.narrative: Land rights registered in and/or linked with LRMIS

comment.narrative: A total of 10,426,698 land rights have been registered and/or linked with LRMIS through mouza digitization, reconstruction, integration of external authorities' records, and parcel mapping. The MTR achievements have exceeded the 2025 target due to improved efficiency and faster processing of approximately 5 million new parcel records since the last reported progress in September 2024. An additional 9.3 million records are expected to be processed and integrated into the LRMIS before the project concludes.

title.narrative: Sites of public lands identified for development programs

comment.narrative: The indicator measures the total number of suitable sites of public lands identified with the project support for development programs. The progress has met the 2025 target and is expected to meet the intermediate and final targets.

title.narrative: Implementation of state lands management procedures

comment.narrative: This indicator measures whether the state lands management procedures are developed. The procedures include 1. identification of state land, 2. digitalization, 3. information sharing for data use by relevant departments, 4. development of a method and tools for semi-automatic update and maintenance of information. The project is on track to meet the end target.

title.narrative: Grievances responded and/or resolved within the stipulated service standards for response times

comment.narrative: The project GRM system is currently functional. In all, 1,353 complaints were received during this reporting period, and all were resolved.
